bounded_statement: Within the supplied files of case:30108f0d34292b11cab8, the workflow enters all 20 weekly rows (four repeated rows per each of the 5 digesters named by the independent-unit column digester_id) as independent Bernoulli trials into an exact binomial test, and the report's selected result (15/20 wins, p = 0.0414 < 0.05) depends on this repeated per-unit entry: collapsing to one entry per independent digester (4 of 5 digesters with majority pretreatment wins) yields an exact two-sided binomial p = 0.375, so the significance claim is not supported at the independent-unit level.

counterevidence_considered.description: The data description itself states 'One trial is: one row', which could be read as authorizing row-level trials; however, this describes what a logged row records, and the same description's independent-unit designation (digester_id) and the explicit within-digester correlation warning make clear that rows are not independent for inference, so this does not license entering each row as an independent trial in a binomial test.

evidence.description: The workflow counts one win per row across all sessions and then feeds the row-level tally into scipy.stats.binomtest with n equal to the number of rows (20), a procedure that assumes each entered trial is independent.

evidence.description: The report explicitly declares every row an independent Bernoulli trial and bases its statistical conclusion on the 20-row binomial test.

source_refs.quoted_text:
Every logged session is treated as one independent Bernoulli trial and the
win tally is tested against a fair-coin null of 0.5 with the exact two-sided
binomial test `scipy.stats.binomtest`.

[selected-result] Exact two-sided binomial test (scipy.stats.binomtest) over 20 weekly sampling sessions: the pretreated train won 15 of 20 sessions, proportion 0.750, p = 0.0414, which is below 0.05, so the log is read as evidence that thermal-hydrolysis pretreatment raises specific methane yield.

evidence.description: The report's own per-digester breakdown shows strong within-unit clustering of outcomes (two digesters win every session, one digester loses three of four), confirming the rows from one digester are not exchangeable independent trials; collapsing to the 5 independent digesters (4 of 5 with majority wins) gives an exact two-sided binomial p of 0.375, so the p<0.05 result exists only through the repeated per-unit entries.
evidence.observed_value: Per-digester wins out of 4: D-01=4, D-02=4, D-03=3, D-04=3, D-05=1; unit-level test binomtest(4,5,0.5) two-sided p = 0.375

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I tried to defeat the finding in three ways. (1) I checked whether the workflow deduplicates or aggregates to one entry per digester before testing: it does not — tally_wins accumulates one win/loss per row and main calls binomtest(wins, n_sessions, ...) with n_sessions = len(sessions) = 20 rows, and the per-digester breakdown is used only for a display table, never for inference. (2) I checked whether the within-digester rows behave as if independent, which would make the repeated entry statistically harmless: they do not — outcomes cluster strongly by digester (D-01 and D-02 win 4/4, D-05 wins 1/4), consistent with the description's warning that a digester's weekly readings move together. (3) I checked whether the conclusion survives analysis at the declared independent-unit level: recomputing with one summary per digester, 4 of 5 digesters show a majority of pretreatment wins, and an exact two-sided binomial test on 4/5 gives p = 0.375 (even a session-count-weighted view cannot rescue p < 0.05 from 5 exchangeable units), so the selected p = 0.0414 conclusion depends entirely on treating the 20 correlated rows as independent trials. All three attempts failed to overturn the finding.

root_cause: The analysis script tallies a win/loss verdict for every weekly session row and passes wins=15, n=20 to scipy.stats.binomtest, a procedure whose validity assumes each of the n trials is independent. Because each digester contributes four rows and the data description states both that digester_id is the independent unit and that readings from the same digester move together (confirmed empirically by the report's own breakdown: D-01 4/4 wins, D-02 4/4 wins, D-05 1/4 wins), the effective sample size is 5 units, not 20 trials; the inflated n manufactures the sub-0.05 p-value that the report reads as evidence for the pretreatment effect.
